title: Rational containment of a split torus homomorphism in a maximal split torus
statement: Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field]. Let $G$ be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] affine finite-type $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] which is geometrically connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] and reductive: after extension to an algebraic closure it has no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup. Here unipotent means that all geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful finite-dimensional representation. Write $\mathbf G_{m,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[z,z^{-1}]$ with multiplication of units. A split torus is a group scheme isomorphic over $k$ to $\mathbf G_{m,k}^r$ for some integer $r\geq0$; a maximal split torus of $G$ is a closed split torus subgroup maximal under inclusion among closed split torus subgroups [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $S\hookrightarrow G$ be a maximal split torus, let $D\simeq\mathbf G_{m,k}^s$, $s\geq0$, be a split torus, and let $f:D\to G$ be a homomorphism of $k$-group schemes. Then there exist $g\in G(k)$ and a homomorphism $v:D\to S$ such that $gfg^{-1}$ equals the composite $D\xrightarrow{v}S\hookrightarrow G$ as morphisms of group schemes. Here $G(B)$ means morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}B\to G$ for a commutative $k$-algebra $B$, with induced group law, and the asserted equality is required after every such algebra extension. Neither perfection nor infinitude nor algebraic closedness of $k$ is assumed. The homomorphism $f$ need not be an embedding; trivial image and inseparable kernels are allowed.

source.place: Theorem 25.10, printed p.546 (rational conjugacy of maximal split tori); Theorem 12.9(b),(c), printed pp.233--234 and Definition 12.14, p.236 (quotients of split tori). Homomorphism form combines these with containment in a maximal split torus. No hypothesis that the field is perfect or algebraically closed.

proof.text: Choose the given split presentation of $D$. The coordinate and finite-type assertions of [lem-trf-lattice-torus-coordinates-action], for $L=\mathbf Z^s$, show that $D$ is affine of finite type. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-homomorphism-flat-image] to $f:D\to G$. This gives an affine finite-type group $I$ and homomorphisms $u:D\to I$, $j:I\hookrightarrow G$ with $f=j\circ u$ and $u$ faithfully flat. Thus [lem-sfb-field-split-torus-flat-quotient] applies to this factorization and makes $I$ a split torus over $k$. In particular $I$ is a closed split torus subgroup of $G$, without replacing $k$ or discarding a nonreduced kernel.

source.place: Theorem 3.34, printed p.75; Theorem 12.9 and Definition 12.14, pp.233--236; Theorem 25.10, p.546. Maximal containment is expanded by a finite-dimension chain argument.

proof.text: The finite-type scheme $G$ has finite Krull dimension by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. For every closed split torus $R\subseteq G$, [lem-trf-lattice-torus-coordinates-action] identifies $k[R]$ with $k[\mathbf Z^r]$. The domain assertion of [lem-trf-split-lattice-torus-projection] (take $K=k$) makes this an integral domain, including $r=0$. Hence $|R|$ is nonempty and irreducible: its zero prime has closure all of its spectrum. Every chain of nonempty irreducible closed subsets of $|R|$ is a chain in $|G|$, so [def-kun-dimension] gives $0\leq\dim R\leq\dim G$. The dimensions of all closed split tori containing $I$ therefore belong to a finite interval of integers.

source.place: Theorem 3.34, printed p.75; Theorem 12.9 and Definition 12.14, pp.233--236; Theorem 25.10, p.546. Maximal containment is expanded by a finite-dimension chain argument.

proof.text: The family in step 2 contains $I$, so choose a member $M$ of greatest dimension. Suppose $M\subsetneq R\subseteq G$ for a closed split torus $R$. The inclusion $M\to R$ is a closed immersion: on the affine $G$ the corresponding quotient maps are $k[G]\to k[G]/J_R\to k[G]/J_M$, since $J_R\subseteq J_M$. By [def-weil-closed-immersion] it is given by an ideal $J$ of the domain $k[R]$. If $|M|=|R|$, then $V(J)=\operatorname{Spec}k[R]$, so its zero prime contains $J$; thus $J=0$ and the inclusion is an isomorphism, contradicting strictness. Hence $|M|$ is a proper closed subset of $|R|$. A longest irreducible closed chain in $|M|$ exists because its finite integer dimension is attained. Append $|R|$ to it; [def-kun-dimension] gives $\dim R\geq\dim M+1$. Since $R$ also contains $I$, this contradicts the choice of $M$. Thus $M$ is a maximal split torus of $G$ containing $I$.

source.place: Theorem 3.34, printed p.75; Theorem 12.9 and Definition 12.14, pp.233--236; Theorem 25.10, p.546. Maximal containment is expanded by a finite-dimension chain argument.

proof.text: The tori $M$ and the prescribed $S$ are maximal split tori of the same smooth geometrically connected reductive affine finite-type group $G$ over $k$. Apply [lem-sfb-field-maximal-split-tori-conjugacy] with $S_1=M$ and $S_2=S$. It gives $g\in G(k)$ for which $c_g|_M:M\xrightarrow{\sim}S$. This is rational conjugacy over the original field, and is an isomorphism of group schemes.

source.place: Theorem 3.34, printed p.75; Theorem 12.9 and Definition 12.14, pp.233--236; Theorem 25.10, p.546. Maximal containment is expanded by a finite-dimension chain argument.

proof.text: Define $v$ to be the composite $D\xrightarrow{u}I\hookrightarrow M\xrightarrow{c_g|_M}S$. It is a homomorphism, and composing it with $S\hookrightarrow G$ gives $c_g\circ j\circ u=c_g\circ f$. The conjugation morphism and its inverse are obtained from multiplication, inverse and the section $g$, using the group identities of [def-sc-group-scheme]. Evaluating the displayed morphism equality on any commutative $k$-algebra $B$ gives $v_B(x)=g_Bf_B(x)g_B^{-1}$ in $G(B)$ for every $x\in D(B)$. No surjectivity of $D(B)\to I(B)$ is used. If $f$ is trivial (in particular if $s=0$), take $g=1$ and the trivial $v$ directly. Inseparable kernels remain allowed by step 1, and neither the dimension argument nor rational conjugacy imposed an extra field hypothesis.
